classification.difficultyReason: Cross-multiply to recognise a cosine sum, solve the resulting multiple-angle equation and filter candidates against the original denominator restrictions.

answer.short:
$x=\dfrac{\pi}{10},\dfrac{3\pi}{10},\dfrac{7\pi}{10},\dfrac{9\pi}{10},\dfrac{11\pi}{10},\dfrac{13\pi}{10},\dfrac{17\pi}{10},\dfrac{19\pi}{10}$.

Use $\cos 5x=0$ and exclude values where $\sin x\cos x=0$.
answer.worked:
The original denominators require $\sin x\ne0$ and $\cos x\ne0$.

$$\begin{align*}\sin 4x\sin x&=\cos 4x\cos x\\\cos 4x\cos x-\sin 4x\sin x&=0\\\cos 5x&=0\\5x&=\frac{\pi}{2}+k\pi\\x&=\frac{(2k+1)\pi}{10},\qquad k=0,1,\ldots,9.\end{align*}$$

Exclude $x=\frac{\pi}{2}$ and $x=\frac{3\pi}{2}$, where $\cos x=0$.

$$x=\frac{\pi}{10},\frac{3\pi}{10},\frac{7\pi}{10},\frac{9\pi}{10},\frac{11\pi}{10},\frac{13\pi}{10},\frac{17\pi}{10},\frac{19\pi}{10}.$$
